category: Schematic capture: Tools/Design/Template/System menu commands, text scripts and model properties
description: Menu-level commands of the Schematic Capture module that the mode-based tools do not cover - Tools (real-time annotation and snap, wire autorouter, Model Compiler, ASCII data import), Design (sheet properties, sheet creation, hierarchy navigation, Design Walk), Template (design defaults, graph colours, graphics/text styles, junction dots, template application) and System (settings, display options, sheet sizes, text editor, keyboard mapping, property definitions) - together with the text-script blocks (*DEFINE, *SPICE, *MODELS, *SCRIPT), the simulator model properties (PRIMITIVE, MODFILE, MODDLL, ITFMOD, SPICEPINS/SPICELIB), netlist output formats, net-class and variant properties, and the report/BOM configuration commands.

tools.name: Tools > Real Time Annotation
tools.description: Toggle (on by default) that annotates components as they are placed - the next free reference for the prefix (R1, R2, U1...) is assigned immediately - so duplicate references never arise during entry. Turned off, parts are placed as R? and annotated later with the Global Annotator, which some users prefer when copying blocks or importing sections.
tools.usage: Tools > Real Time Annotation (tick to enable)
tools.example: Disable it while pasting a Project Clip that carries its own references, then run Tools > Global Annotator > Incremental to number the new parts.
tools.notes: Duplicated references cause netlist errors; the Global Annotator always avoids duplicates.

tools.name: Tools > Real Time Snap
tools.description: Toggle that snaps the cursor to pin ends, wire ends and other hot connection points even when they lie off the current grid, so wires terminate exactly on pins of imported or oddly gridded symbols. Combined with the green 'hot' cursor it makes wiring reliable on mixed-grid sheets.
tools.usage: Tools > Real Time Snap (tick)
tools.example: A part imported from SnapEDA has pins on a 50th grid while the sheet uses 100th; with Real Time Snap on, wires still land on the pins.
tools.notes: Distinct from the View menu snap settings (grid pitch); this snaps to objects.

tools.name: Tools > Wire Auto Router
tools.description: Enables/disables the follow-me wire autorouter: when on, a wire started on a pin routes orthogonally to the next click, hugging objects and adding corners automatically; when off, every corner is placed manually with a click. Ctrl while wiring gives a diagonal segment regardless, and existing wires can be reshaped by dragging corners or straight runs.
tools.usage: Tools > Wire Auto Router (tick to enable); Ctrl+click for a diagonal segment while wiring
tools.example: Turn it off to draw a tidy bus-entry fan-out by hand, then on again for general wiring.
tools.notes: Placing 'anchor' clicks constrains the autorouter path without disabling it.

tools.name: Tools > Model Compiler
tools.description: Compiles the circuit on a child sheet (a subcircuit built from primitives, SPICE parts and other modelled components) into a Model Definition File (.MDF) so it can be attached to a library device through its MODFILE property and reused without the sheet. It is the documented way to turn a proven behavioural or SPICE-level circuit into a distributable Proteus model.
tools.usage: Draw the model circuit as a subcircuit/child sheet with terminals named after the device pins > Tools > Model Compiler > choose the output .MDF path (normally the MODELS directory)

parameters.name: Output file
parameters.description: .MDF written to the models folder listed in System Settings > paths.

tools.example: Build an op-amp macro-model on a child sheet with terminals +, -, OUT, V+, V-; compile to OPX.MDF; give the library symbol MODFILE=OPX.MDF.
tools.notes: Library MDFs such as BIPOLAR.MDF are compiled the same way; 'cannot find model file' errors mean the MODELS path is wrong.

tools.name: Tools > ASCII Data Import (ADI)
tools.description: Bulk-loads component properties from a text file: each record names a part (by reference or by a key property) and lists PROPERTY=VALUE pairs, so stock codes, manufacturer part numbers, costs, tolerances or SPICE model names can be applied to hundreds of parts at once from a spreadsheet export. It is the large-scale alternative to editing parts individually or through the BOM property editor.
tools.usage: Prepare a tab/comma-delimited text file with a header of property names and one row per reference > Tools > ASCII Data Import > select the file > review the log

parameters.name: Key column
parameters.description: Reference (or another unique property) used to match rows to parts.

parameters.name: Property columns
parameters.description: Each further column becomes a property on the matched part.

tools.example: Import STOCKCODE and SUPPLIER for all resistors from an ERP export before generating the BOM.
tools.notes: Property names must exist or be defined in System > Set Property Definitions to appear in BOM fields.

tools.name: Design > Edit Sheet Properties
tools.description: Dialogue for the current sheet: Sheet Title (printed in the header block), Sheet Name (the identifier used for hierarchy and net scoping - different from the title), the sheet's annotation base (initial count, so parts on the sheet start at e.g. R100) and the option to make a sheet the root of a hierarchy. Setting an initial count per sheet guides the Global Annotator during batch annotation.
tools.usage: Design > Edit Sheet Properties > Sheet Title / Sheet Name / Annotation initial count > OK

parameters.name: Sheet Title
parameters.description: Descriptive text for the header block.

parameters.name: Sheet Name
parameters.description: Hierarchy identifier; must be unique.

parameters.name: Initial annotation
parameters.description: Base number for references placed on this sheet.

tools.example: Power sheet: title 'Power Supply', name PSU, initial count 100 - its first resistor becomes R100.
tools.notes: Sheet Name appears in the Design menu's sheet list and in Goto Sheet.

tools.name: Design > New Sheet / Remove Sheet
tools.description: Adds a new root sheet to the design (flat multi-sheet designs connect sheets through identically named terminals) or deletes the current sheet with everything on it. Root sheets are listed at the bottom of the Design menu for switching, and child sheets are created instead through Subcircuit mode.
tools.usage: Design > New Sheet (creates 'Root sheet N'); Design > Remove Sheet (current sheet, after confirmation)
tools.example: Design > New Sheet > Edit Sheet Properties: title 'Analogue Front End'; connect it to sheet 1 with terminals named ADC_IN.
tools.notes: Removing a sheet cannot be undone beyond the undo buffer; save first.

tools.name: Design > Goto Sheet / Zoom to Child / Exit to Parent
tools.description: Hierarchy navigation: Goto Sheet lists every root and child sheet for direct selection; Zoom to Child descends into the child sheet of the selected subcircuit (Ctrl+C on the subcircuit body); Exit to Parent (Ctrl+X) returns to the parent sheet. Root sheets are also listed directly at the bottom of the Design menu.
tools.usage: Design > Goto Sheet > choose > OK; select a subcircuit > Design > Zoom to Child (Ctrl+C); Design > Exit to Parent (Ctrl+X)
tools.example: Select the 'FILTER' subcircuit block, Ctrl+C to edit the filter, Ctrl+X to come back and wire the next stage.
tools.notes: The Design Explorer and Design Walk provide net-oriented navigation across sheets.

tools.name: Design Walk (follow a net across sheets)
tools.description: Introduced in Proteus 8.13: with a wire or terminal selected, PgUp/PgDn (or the context-menu Design Walk commands) jump to the next/previous location of the same net on other sheets, highlighting it, so a signal can be traced through a multi-sheet or hierarchical design without opening the Design Explorer. It also works between schematic and PCB via cross-probing.
tools.usage: Select a wire/terminal > PgDn / PgUp (or right-click > Design Walk next/previous)
tools.example: Select the SPI_CLK terminal on the MCU sheet and press PgDn repeatedly to visit the memory, display and connector sheets it reaches.
tools.notes: Listed on the Design Explorer page as one of its QA features.

tools.name: Diff Pair Configurator (schematic)
tools.description: Added in Proteus 8.14: a dialogue on the schematic that defines differential pairs from a pair of nets (P/N), assigns them to a net class and specifies pass-through components (series capacitors/resistors on the pair lines) that the PCB length-matching and phase-matching calculations must treat as part of the pair. It replaces manual DIFFPAIR property editing and feeds the PCB's differential-pair routing mode.
tools.usage: Schematic > select the two nets (or use the Diff Pair Configurator from the Tools/Design menu) > Add pair > name, positive/negative nets, class, pass-through parts > OK

parameters.name: Positive / Negative net
parameters.description: The two nets forming the pair.

parameters.name: Pass-through components
parameters.description: Series parts whose internal length is included.

parameters.name: Net class
parameters.description: Class with the pair's trace/gap rules in the Design Rule Manager.

tools.example: USB_DP/USB_DM with series 22R pass-through resistors: define the pair, then route it on the PCB with the differential pair mode and check phase offset.
tools.notes: Requires PCB Design Level 2+ for differential pair routing on the layout.

tools.name: CLASS property (net class assignment on the schematic)
tools.description: Net classes group nets that share trace/via styles and design rules on the PCB. Proteus assigns POWER (nets with a power/ground terminal), BUS (nets on a bus) and SIGNAL (everything else) automatically; a custom class is created by placing a wire label whose text is CLASS=<name> on any wire of the net, after which the class appears in the Design Rule Manager's Net Classes tab for its own styles and layer pairs.
tools.usage: Wire Label Mode > click a wire > label text 'CLASS=ANSW' > OK (the label can be hidden); repeat per net or use the Property Assignment Tool

parameters.name: CLASS
parameters.description: Net class name; case-insensitive.

tools.example: CLASS=ANSW on the 5V switched analogue supply, then in the DRM give ANSW trace style T15 and a smaller via than POWER.
tools.notes: Net names themselves come from terminal labels; unnamed power/ground terminals map to VCC/GND.

tools.name: Template > Set Design Defaults
tools.description: Sets the design-wide colours and defaults stored in the template: paper (background) colour, grid dot and highlight colours, default font, wire/bus/pin/hidden-object colours and whether hidden pins/text are shown. It is the first place to change the look of a schematic and is saved with the design and any template made from it.
tools.usage: Template > Set Design Defaults > Colours (Paper, Grid, Work Area Border, Highlight, Hidden Objects...), Default Font, options > OK

parameters.name: Paper colour
parameters.description: Sheet background.

parameters.name: Grid colour / Highlight colour
parameters.description: Editing aids.

parameters.name: Show hidden text/pins
parameters.description: Visibility of hidden objects.

tools.example: Set a white paper colour and black grid dots for printed handouts, then Save Design as Template.
tools.notes: Object-specific line/fill styles are set in Set Graphics Styles; text fonts per style in Set Text Styles.

tools.name: Template > Set Graph Colours
tools.description: Configures the colours used by simulation graphs: graph background, grid, axes, trace colours in sequence (up to the maximum traces), cursor and highlight colours, so that graphs match a corporate style or print legibly. Stored in the template like the other style settings.
tools.usage: Template > Set Graph Colours > pick colours for Background, Grid, Axes, Trace 1..n, Cursors > OK

parameters.name: Trace colours
parameters.description: Colour sequence assigned to traces as they are added.

tools.example: White graph background and dark traces for a report; the Export Graphics of a maximised graph follows these colours.
tools.notes: Individual trace colours can still be overridden in the trace's properties.

tools.name: Template > Set Graphics Styles
tools.description: Opens the Edit Global Graphics Styles dialogue listing every graphics style in the design - component body/pin, wire, bus, terminal, subcircuit, marker, 2D graphics styles and user-defined ones - with line colour/width/style and fill colour/pattern for each. Styles can be created, edited or deleted, and local styles on objects can 'follow global' so a change here restyles the whole design.
tools.usage: Template > Set Graphics Styles > select style (e.g. COMPONENT) > line/fill attributes > New/Delete for custom styles > OK

parameters.name: Style
parameters.description: Global graphics style name.

parameters.name: Line / Fill
parameters.description: Colour, width, dash, fill pattern.

tools.example: Change the COMPONENT style fill to pale yellow and every component body on every sheet updates.
tools.notes: Symbols created with Make Symbol/Make Device can reference global styles rather than fixed colours.

tools.name: Template > Set Text Styles
tools.description: The text counterpart of graphics styles: font face, height, bold/italic/underline, colour and alignment for each global text style (component reference, value, pin name/number, wire label, terminal label, sheet header, 2D text ...). Editing a style reformats all text using it, keeping annotation consistent across a multi-sheet design.
tools.usage: Template > Set Text Styles > choose style (e.g. REFERENCE, VALUE, PIN NAME) > font/height/colour > OK

parameters.name: Font / Height
parameters.description: Typeface and size in the design units.

parameters.name: Colour
parameters.description: Text colour per style.

tools.example: Reduce the VALUE style height to 0.06in so values fit beside 0402 resistors on a dense sheet.
tools.notes: Per-object text can override the style; use 'follow global' to reattach it.

tools.name: Template > Set Junction Dots
tools.description: Sets the shape and size of junction dots (round, square, diamond and size in thou/mm) placed where wires join, so schematics conform to house or standards-body drawing conventions. Applies to all junction dots in the design.
tools.usage: Template > Set Junction Dots > Shape and Size > OK

parameters.name: Shape
parameters.description: Round / square / diamond.

parameters.name: Size
parameters.description: Dot diameter.

tools.example: Set square 30th dots to match an existing company drawing standard before exporting to PDF.
tools.notes: Junction dots are added automatically when a wire ends on another wire; wire-to-wire joins in mid-run need a dot placed first.

tools.name: Template > Apply Styles from Template / Save Design as Template
tools.description: The two commands that move style sets between designs: Apply Styles from Template loads the design defaults, graphics/text styles, graph colours and junction settings of a chosen template file into the current design (optionally with sheet size and header block), and Save Design as Template writes the current design's styles, sheet size, header block/logo and border into a template that the New Project wizard offers thereafter. PCB templates similarly store technology data, board edge and mounting holes.
tools.usage: Template > Apply Styles from Template > select template > options > OK; Template > Save Design as Template > name/path in the Templates folder

parameters.name: Template file
parameters.description: Schematic template in the Templates directory (System Settings > paths).

tools.example: Style a sheet once with the company logo and colours, Save Design as Template 'ACME_A3', then choose it on the New Project wizard's schematic page.
tools.notes: The New Project wizard's 'default template' is what most projects start from; templates also carry 'smart border' grid divisions used by the component placement report.

tools.name: System > System Settings (paths and environment)
tools.description: Global application preferences: the library, models, templates, project-clip and MCAD directories, the number of undo levels, autosave/backup interval and the .pdsbak policy, initial sheet/folder defaults, update-check behaviour and related environment options. Proteus 8 split these across System > Set Paths / Set Environment; Proteus 9 gathers them under System Settings.
tools.usage: System > System Settings (Proteus 9) or System > Set Paths / Set Environment (Proteus 8) > edit paths and options > OK

parameters.name: Library / Models path
parameters.description: Where .LIB/.IDX and .MDF/.DLL model files are searched.

parameters.name: Autosave / backup
parameters.description: Interval and number of backup copies.

parameters.name: Undo levels
parameters.description: Depth of the multi-level undo.

tools.example: Add D:\proteus_libs to the library path so user libraries appear in Pick Devices; add the models folder that holds a vendor's .MDF files.
tools.notes: Model-not-found errors in the Simulation Log are usually a models-path problem.

tools.name: System > Set Display Options
tools.description: Rendering preferences for the editing window: graphics mode (Windows GDI, OpenGL or Direct2D hardware acceleration), highlight animation speed for hot objects, opacity of layers when accelerated, auto-pan distance/steps/time, and in the PCB module the live resist/paste mask display. Choosing an accelerated mode enables layer transparency and smoother zooming on large boards.
tools.usage: System > Set Display Options > Graphics Mode / Highlight animation / Auto-pan / Opacity > OK

parameters.name: Graphics mode
parameters.description: GDI, OpenGL, Direct2D.

parameters.name: Auto-pan
parameters.description: Pan distance, number of steps and pan time.

tools.example: Switch to Direct2D on a laptop with a modern GPU to enable layer opacity and the resist/paste overlay in PCB Layout.
tools.notes: If the display corrupts after a driver update, fall back to Windows GDI here.

tools.name: System > Set Sheet Sizes
tools.description: Defines the dimensions of the sheet sizes A4-A0 (or A-E) offered when editing sheet properties plus a sixth 'User' size that can be any width/height, so oversize or non-standard drawing areas are available. The default work area is A4 (10 x 7 in); pick a larger size or define a User size to gain room without reducing symbol size.
tools.usage: System > Set Sheet Sizes > edit width/height for A4..A0 or User > OK; then Design > Edit Sheet Properties (or the sheet-size control) to apply

parameters.name: A4..A0 / User
parameters.description: Width and height in inches or mm.

tools.example: Set User = 20 x 14 in and select it for a dense single-sheet MCU board.
tools.notes: Sheet size is also stored in templates; the border/header block scales to the sheet.

tools.name: System > Set Text Editor
tools.description: Chooses the font, size and colours used by the internal text editor for scripts, text blocks and the Design Notes, so EasyHDL scripts and SPICE text blocks are readable and consistently formatted.
tools.usage: System > Set Text Editor > font / size / colours > OK
tools.example: Set a monospaced font so *SPICE netlist blocks align in columns.
tools.notes: Source-code editing for firmware uses the VSM Studio editor, configured separately.

tools.name: System > Set Keyboard Mapping
tools.description: The Keyboard Mapping dialogue lists every command and operation mode grouped by menu and lets each be assigned, changed or removed as a keyboard accelerator, with export/import of the mapping so a custom layout can be shared. Because shortcuts are user-configurable, the defaults quoted in tutorials (e.g. R for Route Command Centre, Shift+P push mode) may not apply on a customised install.
tools.usage: System > Set Keyboard Mapping > select command group and command > Assign key > Export/Import mapping > OK

parameters.name: Command / key
parameters.description: Any menu command or mode mapped to a key combination.

tools.example: Map 'Simulate Graph' to F5 and 'Toggle Grid' to G for a keyboard-driven workflow.
tools.notes: Available in both schematic and PCB modules with separate maps.

tools.name: System > Set Property Definitions
tools.description: Maintains the global list of property definitions - name, description, type (string, integer, float, boolean, hidden) and default - that appear in Edit Component dialogues, BOM fields and the Property Assignment Tool. Defining STOCKCODE, SUPPLIER, MPN, COST, ROHS and similar here makes them selectable everywhere instead of typed ad hoc.
tools.usage: System > Set Property Definitions > New > Name, Description, Type, Default > OK

parameters.name: Name / Type
parameters.description: Property identifier and data type.

parameters.name: Description
parameters.description: Label shown in dialogues and BOM headers.

tools.example: Define ROHS (boolean, 'RoHS Compliant') so Make Device and the BOM offer it as a column.
tools.notes: The BOM module's Edit BOM Fields creates definitions too; ASCII Data Import needs them to exist.

tools.name: Text Script Mode (script blocks)
tools.description: The mode (left toolbar) for placing free-text script blocks whose first line selects their type: *DEFINE (property/default definitions), *SPICE (raw SPICE cards passed to ProSPICE), *MODELS (SPICE .MODEL/.SUBCKT definitions), *SCRIPT ... *ENDSCRIPT (EasyHDL) and other directives documented in the reference manual. Scripts are part of the sheet, netlisted with it, and let SPICE models be developed and tested in native format without library edits.
tools.usage: Text Script Mode > click on the sheet > type the block starting with its directive line > OK

parameters.name: Directive
parameters.description: First line: *DEFINE, *SPICE, *MODELS, *SCRIPT GENERATOR/PROGRAM.

tools.example:
*MODELS
.MODEL MYDIODE D(IS=1e-14 N=1.05 RS=0.5 CJO=10p)
then give a diode symbol PRIMITIVE=ANALOG,DIODE and MODEL=MYDIODE.
tools.notes: Script text uses the font from System > Set Text Editor; syntax errors surface at netlist time in the Simulation Log.

tools.name: *DEFINE script (sheet-level property and variable definitions)
tools.description: A text script beginning *DEFINE that declares NAME=VALUE lines applying to the sheet (and its children): default component properties, symbolic values referenced by other properties (e.g. VCC=5, FCLK=16MHz) and sweep variables. Properties on parts can then use the names, giving one place to change a value used throughout the design or to parameterise a subcircuit.
tools.usage: Text Script Mode > '*DEFINE' on line 1 > NAME=VALUE per line

parameters.name: NAME=VALUE
parameters.description: One definition per line; values may use SI suffixes.

tools.example:
*DEFINE
RLOAD=100
FCLK=8MHz
then set a resistor's value to <RLOAD> and the MCU clock to <FCLK>.
tools.notes: Definitions are scoped to the sheet hierarchy they sit in; a *DEFINE on a child sheet overrides the parent's.

tools.name: *SPICE script (raw SPICE cards)
tools.description: A text script beginning *SPICE whose remaining lines are passed verbatim to the ProSPICE netlist: element cards (R1 N1 N2 1k), .MODEL/.SUBCKT definitions, .PARAM, .INCLUDE/.LIB lines and .OPTIONS. Net names on the schematic are addressed directly, so a circuit fragment or a vendor model can be simulated in native SPICE syntax alongside the drawn schematic - the fastest way to test third-party models before wrapping them in a library part.
tools.usage: Text Script Mode > '*SPICE' on line 1 > SPICE cards referencing schematic net names

parameters.name: Cards
parameters.description: Any SPICE3F5-compatible lines; node names are schematic net names.

tools.example:
*SPICE
.INCLUDE opa2277.lib
XU5 IN+ IN- VCC VEE OUT OPA2277
(with IN+, IN-, VCC, VEE, OUT being wire labels on the sheet)
tools.notes: Use 'Log netlist(s)' on a graph to see how the cards merged into the SDF netlist.

tools.name: *MODELS script (.MODEL and .SUBCKT definitions)
tools.description: A text script beginning *MODELS that holds SPICE .MODEL and .SUBCKT definitions visible to every part on the design, so a component whose SPICEMODEL/MODEL property names one of them resolves without an external SPICEFILE. It keeps small custom models inside the project file and is handy for parameter tweaking during design.
tools.usage: Text Script Mode > '*MODELS' on line 1 > .MODEL / .SUBCKT ... .ENDS blocks

parameters.name: .MODEL / .SUBCKT
parameters.description: Standard SPICE definitions.

tools.example:
*MODELS
.SUBCKT RCFILT IN OUT
R1 IN OUT 10k
C1 OUT 0 100n
.ENDS
with a subcircuit symbol using SPICEMODEL=RCFILT and SPICEPINS=IN,OUT.
tools.notes: Models placed in a library .LIB/.MDF are preferred for reuse across projects; *MODELS is project-local.

tools.name: PRIMITIVE property (simulator primitive selection)
tools.description: Hidden device property that binds a schematic symbol directly to a built-in simulator primitive instead of an MDF/DLL model, in the form PRIMITIVE=ANALOG,<type> (RESISTOR, CAPACITOR, INDUCTOR, DIODE, NPN, PNP, NMOS, PMOS, NJFET, VSOURCE, ISOURCE, ...) or PRIMITIVE=DIGITAL,<type> (AND_2, NAND_3, OR_2, XOR, INVERTER, DTFF, JKFF, LATCH, COUNTER, ...) and mixed-mode primitives. Combined with MODEL=<name> for SPICE primitives it is how every library passive, discrete and basic gate is modelled, and how Make Device attaches a model to a new symbol.
tools.usage: Make Device > Component Properties & Definitions > add PRIMITIVE = ANALOG,DIODE (plus MODEL=<spice model name>) or DIGITAL,AND_2; or Edit Component > add the property

parameters.name: Class
parameters.description: ANALOG, DIGITAL or MIXED.

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description: Primitive name recognised by the simulator.

parameters.name: MODEL
parameters.description: SPICE model name for analogue primitives (from *MODELS, a .MDF or the model library).

tools.example: Custom LED symbol: PRIMITIVE=ANALOG,DIODE, MODEL=LED-RED gives it the library LED's electrical behaviour.
tools.notes: Digital primitives take timing properties (propagation delays) as further hidden properties; the reference manual lists the full primitive set.

tools.name: MODFILE property (.MDF model attachment)
tools.description: Property naming the Model Definition File (.MDF) that implements a device - a compiled subcircuit produced by Tools > Model Compiler or shipped in the MODELS directory (BIPOLAR.MDF, OPAMP.MDF, 7400.MDF ...). At netlist time the MDF's contents are expanded in place of the symbol, with the symbol's pin names mapped to the MDF's terminals and the symbol's other properties substituted into the model's parameters.
tools.usage: Edit Component / Make Device > MODFILE = MYMODEL.MDF (searched on the models path); pins must match the MDF terminal names

parameters.name: File name
parameters.description: .MDF in the models path or a full path.

tools.example: A custom power module: child-sheet circuit compiled to PSU.MDF, symbol given MODFILE=PSU.MDF with pins VIN, VOUT, GND.
tools.notes: 'cannot find model file' in the log means the models path in System Settings does not include the folder.

tools.name: MODDLL property (VSM DLL model attachment)
tools.description: Property naming the compiled VSM model DLL (built with the VSM SDK against vsm.hpp) that implements a component's behaviour - every microcontroller, LCD, memory, sensor and instrument model is attached this way (e.g. MODDLL=PIC16.DLL, LCDALPHA.DLL, COMPIM.DLL). The DLL exports the create/delete entry points for the model class and receives the instance's pins and properties through IINSTANCE.
tools.usage: Make Device > properties > MODDLL = MYMODEL.DLL (placed in the MODELS directory); optional further properties consumed by the model via IINSTANCE::getstrval/getdelval

parameters.name: DLL name
parameters.description: Model DLL in the models path.

parameters.name: Model-specific properties
parameters.description: Read by the DLL at setup (e.g. baud rate for COMPIM, initial contents for memories).

tools.example: Custom 4-digit display model: build DISP4.DLL with createactivemodel/deleteactivemodel entry points, give the symbol MODDLL=DISP4.DLL, set its pin electrical types in Make Device, and add a DIGITS=4 property that the DLL reads with IINSTANCE::getdelval at setup.
tools.notes: See the VSM SDK entries in the simulation category for the interfaces; a DLL built for the wrong Proteus major version fails to load with a 'model version' error.

tools.name: ITFMOD property (mixed-mode interface model)
tools.description: Property selecting the analogue/digital interface model applied at the boundary between a digital primitive/DLL model and the analogue nets it connects to: it sets logic thresholds, output high/low voltages, rise/fall times and drive impedance per logic family (TTL, LSTTL, CMOS, HC, HCT ...) or per supply-rail pair. Library parts set ITFMOD automatically from their family; custom models specify it so their pins interact with SPICE parts correctly.
tools.usage: Make Device / Edit Component > ITFMOD = HC (or TTL, CMOS, ...); rail voltages taken from Configure Power Rails / VCC-GND properties

parameters.name: Family
parameters.description: Interface model name defining voltage levels and timing.

parameters.name: Supply nets
parameters.description: Rails used for logic-level scaling (e.g. VDD/VSS via the model's power pins).

tools.example: A 3.3V CMOS custom model driving a 5V TTL gate: ITFMOD=CMOS with VDD=3.3 shows a marginal high level the analogue gate input rejects - the same failure hardware would show.
tools.notes: Fully documented in the VSM/SDK reference under mixed-mode simulation; mismatched ITFMOD is a common cause of 'digital part does not respond' with analogue drive.

tools.name: SPICEPINS and SPICELIB properties (SPICE subcircuit pin mapping)
tools.description: Companions to SPICEMODEL/SPICEFILE when attaching a vendor .SUBCKT: SPICEPINS lists the schematic pin names in the order of the subcircuit's node list (so the symbol's pins map onto the model's ports), and SPICELIB (or SPICEFILE) names the library file containing the definition, searched on the models path. Together they let the Model Import wizard's result be understood or hand-edited.
tools.usage: Edit Component > add SPICEMODEL=<subckt name>, SPICEFILE/SPICELIB=<file>, SPICEPINS=<pin1,pin2,...> in subckt node order

parameters.name: SPICEPINS
parameters.description: Comma-separated schematic pin names in .SUBCKT port order.

parameters.name: SPICELIB / SPICEFILE
parameters.description: Library file holding the .SUBCKT/.MODEL.

tools.example: OPA2277 subckt ports '+IN -IN V+ V- OUT': SPICEPINS=IN+,IN-,VCC,VEE,OUT on a generic op-amp symbol.
tools.notes: Wrong pin order is the most frequent import error - the log shows the expanded X card to check against.

tools.name: Netlist Compiler output formats (SDF and third-party netlists)
tools.description: Tools > Netlist Compiler writes the design's connectivity in Proteus's own SDF format (the netlist consumed by the simulator and the PCB module) or in third-party formats for other layout/simulation tools - the dialogue offers a format list that includes SPICE, SPICE-AGE, Tango, Racal/Redac, Boardmaker, Eagle, Futurenet, Multiwire, Scicards, Vutrax and similar legacy formats - with options for scope (whole design/current sheet), hierarchy depth and whether to include hidden pins/power nets.
tools.usage: Tools > Netlist Compiler > Output (File/Viewer), Mode (Physical/Logical), Scope, Depth, Format > OK

parameters.name: Format
parameters.description: SDF (native) or a third-party netlist format from the list.

parameters.name: Mode / Scope / Depth
parameters.description: Physical vs logical netlist, current sheet or whole design, hierarchy levels flattened.

tools.example: Export a SPICE netlist of the analogue front end to run in another SPICE tool; or generate the SDF to inspect exactly what the simulator sees.
tools.notes: Confirm the exact format list in your release's dialogue - it has been trimmed over versions. Netlisting to the Proteus PCB module is normally live and needs no explicit export.

tools.name: Batch-mode netlisting (live netlist off)
tools.description: By default the schematic and PCB share a live netlist - every wiring change updates the layout's ratsnest immediately and the layout's connectivity status shows pending changes. Live netlisting can be disabled so the PCB is updated only when the netlist is explicitly transferred (batch mode), which some users prefer on very large designs or when many schematic edits are in progress; some layout functions that need the live netlist are then unavailable until the transfer.
tools.usage: System / project settings > untick live netlisting (Proteus 8: Tools > Netlist to ARES on demand); re-enable to return to live mode
tools.example: Restructure a 12-sheet schematic in batch mode, then transfer the netlist once and use Manage Changes in the PCB to review the differences.
tools.notes: Batch mode hides some menu functionality that depends on a live netlist; the Getting Started guide notes it 'may provide a useful tool' on large designs.

tools.name: Exclude from Active Variant and @VARIANT (assembly-variant properties)
tools.description: Per-part control of assembly variants outside the Design Explorer grid: the Edit Component check box 'Exclude from Active Variant' marks the part not fitted in the variant currently selected in the variant combo box (part reference greys out), and the text string @VARIANT placed on the sheet prints the active variant's name. Variant properties (alternate values, stock codes) per variant were added in 8.8, and the BOM, pick-and-place, assembly drawings, 3D Viewer and MCAD exports all honour the fitted status.
tools.usage: Variant combo (top toolbar) > choose variant; Edit Component > tick 'Exclude from Active Variant'; 2D Text > '@VARIANT'

parameters.name: Active Variant
parameters.description: Variant selected in the combo box.

parameters.name: Exclude from Active Variant
parameters.description: Not-fitted flag for the part in that variant.

tools.example: Create variant BUDGET in the Design Explorer, exclude U3 (SHT15) and its pull-ups, and the BOM for BUDGET drops them automatically.
tools.notes: Variants never alter the 2D PCB copper - only fitted status and per-variant properties.

tools.name: Datasheet property (download server/path)
tools.description: Library parts can carry a datasheet reference made of a Download Server (e.g. https://ww1.microchip.com), a Download Path (downloads/en/DeviceDoc/) and the PDF file name; the Edit Component dialogue then shows a Data button that opens or downloads the datasheet. Set it in Make Device so users of your library parts get one-click documentation.
tools.usage: Make Device > Datasheet page > Download Server, Download Path, Filename (or a local path); Edit Component > Data button to open

parameters.name: Download Server / Path / File
parameters.description: URL components assembled into the download link.

tools.example: MCP23008: server ww1.microchip.com, path downloads/en/DeviceDoc/, file MCP23008-MCP23S08-Data-Sheet-20001919F.pdf.
tools.notes: Many shipped parts already have datasheets configured; local paths can point at a shared drive.

tools.name: BOM Fields and Categories (Edit BOM Fields)
tools.description: Configuration of the Bill of Materials report: Categories group parts by reference prefix (R = Resistors, C = Capacitors, U = Integrated Circuits, custom prefixes) and Fields define the report columns, each bound to a component property (Value, Package, STOCKCODE, SUPPLIER, COST, MOQ, ROHS...) with a type and description; both are edited from the left-hand panel of the BOM tab and the Add button opens the Edit BOM Fields dialogue. The Property Editor tab is a grid where the field values are typed directly and the schematic updates live.
tools.usage: BOM tab > left panel > Categories: Add/Edit/Delete; Fields: Add (Edit BOM Fields: Property name, Description, Type) > Property Editor tab to fill values > Apply

parameters.name: Category prefix
parameters.description: Reference prefix mapped to a heading.

parameters.name: Field property / type
parameters.description: Property name and String/Integer/Float/Boolean type.

tools.example: Add field SUPPLIER (String) and type 'Farnell' for all resistors in the Property Editor; the WYSIWYG report gains a Supplier column.
tools.notes: Output via the export icons (print, HTML, Excel, PDF, CSV); stylesheet customisation is available from the HTML view. Variants change which parts are listed.

tools.name: Project Notes reports (Manufacturing, Variant Comparison, Design Rule, Single Pin Net, Length Match, Differential Pair, Component Placement)
tools.description: The Project Notes module (documentation centre) can generate structured reports with data imported automatically from the design: PCB Manufacturing Report (stackup, drill table, finishes), Variant Comparison Report, Design Rule Report, Single Pin Net Report, Length Matching Report and Differential Pairs Report (added in 8.10), the Component Placement Report listing each reference against the schematic border grid (8.11), and board-specific reports for multi-board projects (8.13). Reports are edited as rich text and can be included with CADCAM output notes.
tools.usage: Project Notes tab > Insert/Generate report > choose report type > edit text > export/print; CADCAM Output > Notes tab > include manufacturing notes

parameters.name: Report type
parameters.description: One of the generated report templates.

parameters.name: Board (multi-board)
parameters.description: Which board the report covers.

tools.example: Generate the PCB Manufacturing Report and the Length Matching Report and attach both to the Gerber X2 fileset for the fab house.
tools.notes: Reports refresh from the current design state; regenerate after layout changes.

tools.name: Grid, snap, origin and X-cursor (View menu)
tools.description: Editing aids on the View menu: Toggle Grid (G) shows/hides grid dots, the snap commands set the cursor pitch (10/50/100/500 thou or metric equivalents; M toggles imperial/metric), Origin (O) relocates the coordinate origin to the cursor for relative measurements, and X-Cursor shows a large cross at the snapped position. Redraw, Pan and the zoom commands (Zoom In/Out/All/Area, F6-F8) complete the menu.
tools.usage: View > Toggle Grid (G) / Snap 10th..500th (Ctrl+F1..F4) / Origin (O) / X-Cursor (X) / Zoom In (F6), Zoom Out (F7), Zoom All (F8)

parameters.name: Snap
parameters.description: Cursor pitch; parts and wires align to it.

parameters.name: Origin
parameters.description: Temporary origin for the coordinate readout.

tools.example: Set snap 50th to place a 0.05in-pitch imported symbol, then back to 100th for wiring.
tools.notes: Shortcut letters can differ if the keyboard map has been customised. The PCB module has its own grid configuration under Technology.
